what_happened.line: The committee voted 6-3 to change 'Board of Selectmen' to 'select board' in the Charter and send the change to voters.
A motion to include a minimum write-in vote number in the Charter failed 5-4, short of the supermajority it needed.
Members debated whether the town clerk should be elected or appointed; the motion was withdrawn pending counsel's view on grandfathering, so nothing was decided.
The committee passed wording changes on filling vacancies on appointed multiple member bodies (sections 7.8 and 7.10); the audio does not capture the Parks Commission vote.
For Town Meeting, the committee plans to present two groups of changes as one article each and every red item as its own article.

why_it_matters: The select board name change and any other Charter amendments that reach Town Meeting or the ballot are votes residents will be asked to take, and the write-in rule will not be among them unless the committee revisits it.

How the town clerk is chosen, and whether Finance Committee members must be registered voters or only residents, stay unsettled until counsel responds, so those questions may still change what appears in front of voters.

meetings.headline: Charter committee heard public comment on draft charter changes and voted only to adopt counsel's wording for a second town meeting.
meetings.summary: The committee approved two sets of prior minutes, then held a public hearing on the proposed charter changes. Discussion covered the select board name, an elected versus appointed town clerk, committee member eligibility, cemetery and parks commission control of town facilities, and write-in vote thresholds. The one substantive vote adopted counsel's preferred language for a second annual town meeting. The other items were left for later meetings and the February public hearing.

what_happened.line: The Charter Review Committee voted unanimously to add counsel's preferred wording for a second annual town meeting to the draft charter.
The committee held a public hearing on the draft charter changes; the other items were referred to later meetings without a vote.
Speakers urged keeping the town clerk elected and questioned renaming the Board of Selectmen the select board.
Speakers on the cemetery and parks commissions raised control of facilities, a separate cemetery building and equipment, insurance and cost, and commission size.
Speakers also raised committee eligibility rules and a minimum write-in vote for election; the chair will ask counsel whether an appointed clerk would be union.

why_it_matters: The draft charter sets how the town is governed: whether the clerk is elected, who controls town facilities, and who may serve on committees. Changes are expected to reach residents as a vote.
Cemetery and parks commission control of facilities could affect town insurance and equipment costs, which are paid mostly from taxes.
watch_next: Committee meetings on the 13th and the 27th, with the public hearing on February 27, where the committee plans to finalize the draft after deliberating the listed public comments.
Town counsel's answer on whether an appointed town clerk would be union or non-union.
